requiresIsolation.description: Isolation properties this claim DEPENDS ON, compared claim-relatively against evidence.environment.isolationBoundary (#134). Required and matched -> may reach rung 4. Required but absent (e.g. a host run, which claims no isolation) -> unknown, capped below rung 4. Required and explicitly NOT claimed by the run -> the evidence does not apply at all. ⚠️ Absent or empty means this claim does not turn on isolation, and NO penalty follows: a claim that never asked about containment is not weakened for failing to have it. ⚠️ This is why there is no tier-to-confidence ceiling. Sandbox tier is a PERMISSION and an execution boundary, not an epistemic rank: a host run can legitimately reach `environment-matched` for a claim about that host, and tier 1 cannot lift an OS-containment claim merely because a virtual environment existed.

title.description: Short human label. Not an identifier.

statement.description: The condition, stated so that passing or failing it requires no judgment call. ⚠️ Stage 7's exit criterion is exactly this property, so a statement that reads 'the handoff should be good' is not a criterion — it is a wish with an ID.

evaluates.description: The component this criterion tests. Required and non-empty: a criterion that evaluates nothing cannot be run, and it is the edge #60's cascade traverses — its worked example is `acceptance-criterion -> component`. Valid trace target type: component.

items.description: One trace edge. Deliberately just an ID: the RELATIONSHIP is supplied by the field name that holds it, not by a value inside it. Named as its own primitive so every trace field in every schema refers to one concept.

verifies.description: The requirement this criterion demonstrates. Separate from `evaluates` because the two answer different questions — WHAT is being tested versus WHY it matters — and the handoff slice pulls the traced requirement along with the criterion (#19). Valid trace target type: requirement.

items.description: One trace edge. Deliberately just an ID: the RELATIONSHIP is supplied by the field name that holds it, not by a value inside it. Named as its own primitive so every trace field in every schema refers to one concept.

outcome.description: ⚠️ A RECORDED JUDGEMENT, not a derivation, and the distinction is deliberate. `assertion`'s verdict is derived because an evidence graph determines it (#96); a criterion's outcome is determined by somebody running it and looking. Deriving it from `evidencedBy` would require the polarity machinery assertions already have, and would make an acceptance criterion a second, weaker assertion. ⚠️ `not-evaluated` is the default and is a real state: a criterion that exists and has never been run is exactly what distinguishes a component that is IMPLEMENTED from one that is ACCEPTED (QST-0015).

evidencedBy.description: What was observed when it was evaluated. Optional on a `pass` because a criterion may be self-evident from the artifact graph; REQUIRED in substance on a `fail` (see the conditional), because a failure that records nothing cannot be acted on. Valid trace target type: evidence.

tags.description: Changing tags never invalidates an approval (#103).

title.description: Short human label. Not an identifier.

statement.description: What is to be done, stated so that a recipient could start without asking what was meant. Same field name as every other type's payload (#82).

role.description: Who does it, BY ROLE and never by name (#18). ⚠️ A string rather than a link to a `role-assignment` artifact, and stage 8 is where that was settled: #18 says roles are DISCOVERED from task assignments and there is no roster to maintain, so the set of roles on a project is derived by collecting these values. An artifact holding this string plus an identity would store what a traversal derives — the same refusal as #138's tool signatures, #141's runbook aggregate and #143's roster.

implements.description: The component this task builds. Required and non-empty: a task that implements nothing is the orphan the stage-9 completeness gate looks for. Valid trace target type: component.

fulfils.description: The requirements this task serves. Stage 8's `tasks-trace-to-requirement` criterion reads exactly this, which is what makes it mechanical rather than a reading of prose. Valid trace target type: requirement.

The lint is the right place to notice the absence. Valid trace target type: acceptance-criterion.
